query: How do recent papers evaluate reasoning in large language models?

context_chunks.text:
Evaluating Multi-Step Reasoning, Evidence Selection, Citation Grounding, and Hallucination Controls in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Scientific Literature Review Across Benchmarks, Research Domains, Reporting Standards, and Human Evaluation Protocols

Recent papers evaluate reasoning in large language models with step-level scores. Reasoning benchmarks score intermediate steps rather than the final answer alone. This study compares evidence selection methods used when language models answer research questions. The evaluation covers citation checks, abstention, and human review of model traces. Additional analysis looks at how retrieval depth changes the measured reasoning quality across scientific domains and reporting styles. Reviewers also score whether each cited sentence is supported by the retrieved passage.

metadata.title: Evaluating Multi-Step Reasoning, Evidence Selection, Citation Grounding, and Hallucination Controls in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Scientific Literature Review Across Benchmarks, Research Domains, Reporting Standards, and Human Evaluation Protocols

context_chunks.text:
Retrieval Systems That Select Evidence Before Answering

Retrieval systems select evidence before a language model writes. The paper measures whether the selected passage actually supports the claim. Recent evaluations of reasoning treat unsupported sentences as errors even when the final label is correct. A second experiment varies how many passages are shown to the model and records the change in citation precision.

metadata.title: Retrieval Systems That Select Evidence Before Answering

context_chunks.text:
Hallucination Checks for Cited Answers

Hallucination checks compare a cited sentence with the source passage. Large language models can sound confident when the passage does not contain the claim. The method flags those sentences for review and keeps the ones a reader can verify.

answer.answer: Recent papers evaluate reasoning by scoring intermediate steps and checking that each citation is supported by the retrieved passage.
answer.summary: Recent papers evaluate reasoning in large language models by scoring intermediate steps and checking that cited sentences match the retrieved evidence.
